**Smash Mouth** is an American rock band from San Jose, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-3) The band was formed in 1994[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-4) and was originally composed of Steve Harwell (lead vocals), Kevin Coleman (drums), Greg Camp (guitar), and Paul De Lisle (bass). Harwell's departure in 2021 left De Lisle as the sole remaining original member. They are known for their songs "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" (1997), "All Star" (1999),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-5) and "Then the Morning Comes" (1999), as well as [a cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer_(Smash_Mouth_song) "I'm a Believer (Smash Mouth song)") of Neil Diamond's "[I'm a Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer "I'm a Believer")" (2001).

The band adopted retro styles covering several decades of popular music. They have also performed numerous covers of popular songs, including War's "[Why Can't We Be Friends?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends%3F_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends? (song)")", Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up", Simple Minds' "[Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_(Forget_About_Me) "Don't You (Forget About Me)")", ? & the Mysterians' "[Can't Get Enough of You Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Get_Enough_of_You_Baby "Can't Get Enough of You Baby")", the Beatles' "Getting Better", Queen's "Under Pressure", House of Pain's "Jump Around", and "[I Wan'na Be Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wan'na_Be_Like_You "I Wan'na Be Like You")" from _The Jungle Book_. They also composed two songs for the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_: "Beside Myself" and "Everything Just Crazy".
The group's debut album _Fush Yu Mang_ has been certified platinum twice by the RIAA and their second album _Astro Lounge_ has since been certified platinum thrice. Their song "All Star" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 2001.
Smash Mouth's roots trace back to 1990 when Steve Harwell and Kevin Coleman met. Smash Mouth was then formed in 1994 by Harwell, who had formerly played in a rap group called F.O.S. (Freedom of Speech). Coleman, who was Harwell's manager, knew guitarist Greg Camp and bassist Paul De Lisle, who had both played in a local punk band, and introduced the three musicians to each other. They began rehearsing together along with Coleman, who played drums. They soon developed into a band, and named themselves Smashmouth, an American football term. During their early years, the band played largely rock music.

The band's first publicity came when a demo of the song "Nervous in the Alley" was played by a San Jose radio station, KOME. Soon after, Interscope Records signed the band, and the group's debut album, _Fush Yu Mang_, was released in 1997, featuring another member: the keyboardist Michael Klooster. Also, upon signing to Interscope Records, the band changed their name from Smashmouth to Smash Mouth. The album saw commercial success peaking at number 19 on the US Billboard 200 and number 23 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6) It was led by the band's first major single "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" which peaked at number 1 on the US Adult Top 40 and Alternative Songs charts and at number 3 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-7) The singles "The Fonz" and a cover of "[Why Can't We Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends (song)")" from the 1998 Kevin Bacon film _Wild Things_ were also subsequently released. The album has since gone double platinum. During this time the band officially started touring regularly even opening for U2 on their PopMart Tour and got their first television appearance as the musical guest on episode 157 of _Oddville, MTV._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-8)

### 1998–2004: rise to fame, _Astro Lounge_, _Smash Mouth_, and _Get the Picture?_
[edit | edit source]
The band's second album, _Astro Lounge_, was released in 1999 and marked a change in direction, as it had less of the previous ska influence and more of a pop sound. It led to more publicity for the band, and ended up being one of the most critically acclaimed albums from the group. It peaked at number 6 on the US Billboard 200, the highest the band has ever charted in the states, and reached the top 20 in both Canada and New Zealand.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-9) Supported by the hit single "All Star" (which was featured in several film soundtracks, most notably in _Shrek_ (2001), although the official music video references _Mystery Men_) the song reached number 4 on both the Billboard hot 100 and Australia it then charted even higher in Canada peaking at number 2.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-10) "Then the Morning Comes" was also a hit for the band and peaked a number 11 on the Billboard hot 100.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)_Astro Lounge_ has since been certified as triple platinum.

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
In June 2011, a writer at Something Awful offered $20 if the band's lead singer, Steve Harwell, would eat 24 eggs.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Hendren_2011-27) Others on Twitter began offering additional sums, eventually targeted to various charities.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Hendren_2011-27) In July 2011, Harwell accepted the challenge if fans could gather pledges of $10,000 for [St. Jude Children's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Jude_Children's_Hospital "St. Jude Children's Hospital").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-28) The fundraising goal was reached in less than a week.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-29) A self-styled "reality TV fan", Harwell requested that his friend celebrity chef Guy Fieri prepare the eggs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-30) The event was held at Johnny Garlic's restaurant, in Dublin, California, on October 11, 2011. With about 150 people attending, Harwell was able to finish the eggs with the help of audience members as well as the San Jose Sharks mascot, Sharkie. $15,000 was raised for charity.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-31)
On July 17, 2011, Smash Mouth performed live at the Hard Rock Cafe on the Vegas Strip, airing a 60-minute concert simultaneously across the US & Canada on HDNet Television, CBS Radio, and CBS Digital.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-32)
Smash Mouth at Kinser Fest in 2013

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
After parting ways with Universal Records and signing with 429 Records, Smash Mouth released their sixth studio album titled _Magic_, on September 4, 2012. The album was primarily produced by new band member Mike Krompass. The first single, also entitled "Magic", debuted on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart at No. 22.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-33) The band spent the rest of 2012 touring behind the new project as well as promoting the release of their musical book of food recipes and things of the like — _Recipes from the Road_. Cooke temporarily left again toward the end of 2012, replaced by Paxson. In 2013 the band took part in the "Under the Sun" tour with Gin Blossoms and Sugar Ray.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-34) Paxson left in July during the tour, and was initially going to be replaced by a returning Cooke; however, he was replaced by Sutter once again. Tod Burr, former drum tech of Def Leppard and drummer of Merle Jagger, came on board in 2012 as drum and keyboard tech of Smash Mouth.
On February 1, 2013, Smash Mouth headlined the AutoNation Coast to Coast rebranding event (which combined all AutoNation dealerships into a single brand) at Wayne Huizenga Park in Fort Lauderdale, Florida with Michela Paige from Season 3 of _The Voice_. The event also served as a final round in the AutoNation Culture of Caring Contest. They also took part in the first "Under the Sun" tour alongside Sugar Ray, Gin Blossoms, and Vertical Horizon.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-35)
On October 6, 2014, Smash Mouth composed two songs for the English version of the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_, including "Beside Myself", and "Everything Just Crazy" which plays at the end credits.

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
In 2014, Smash Mouth was part of the second "Under the Sun" tour with Uncle Kracker, Blues Traveler, and Sugar Ray.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-36)
On June 14, 2015, Smash Mouth performed at the Taste of Fort Collins food festival in Fort Collins, Colorado. Before the encore, in an incident that lasted about three minutes, singer Steve Harwell became angry, yelled profanities at the audience, and left the stage after bread that had been distributed by the festival was thrown in the air and a few pieces were reportedly thrown onto the stage.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-37) Harwell later apologized for the incident in an interview with _The Herald-Mail_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-38) Event organizer Jason Ornstein explained that he asked Harwell if he wanted him to have the DJs make an announcement instructing the crowd not to throw bread but according to Ornstein, Harwell "stormed on [stage] and took matters into his own hands". He continued "It wasn't like anyone was going to be getting hurt by throwing bread up in the air ... We just had to laugh at it, because he just really made a fool of himself."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Sexton_2015-39) Fort Collins Police Services stated laws prohibiting disorderly conduct, harassment, and "throwing of "missiles", i.e. objects, apply to event attendees.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Sexton_2015-39)
In May 2016, Smash Mouth released their first live album titled _Playlist: The Very Best of Smash Mouth_ through Sony Music. The recordings were harvested from shows in Rapid City, South Dakota, and Manila.

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
2016 saw the band gain a new member in Sam Eigen and the return of Cooke. Eigen is a long-time friend of both Steve Harwell and Paul De Lisle, and has played with Alanis Morissette, Janet Jackson, and John Fogerty. He can also be heard playing guitar on several of Harwell's solo recordings over the years.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-40)
Smash Mouth performed at the Urbana Sweetcorn Festival on August 28, 2016; Harwell passed out in the middle of the set and was taken to a nearby hospital, but the band continued their set and performed the song without him. Harwell made a full recovery and they continued touring.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-41)
Greg Camp rejoined Smash Mouth in early 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-42) An acoustic re-recording of Smash Mouth's first album, _Fush Yu Mang_, funded through PledgeMusic was released in 2018 for the album's 20th anniversary.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-43)

### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
On November 6, 2023, the band announced their second Christmas album, _Missile Toes_, which released on November 17. The album consists of 10 songs, six of which are covers of classic Christmas songs, and four of which are originals. Featured artists Susanna Hoffs and Sophie Grey make appearances.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-62)
Zach Goode during a show in Orlando, Florida in 2025
On April 12, 2024, Smash Mouth released the single and video "Ride On", and on July 12, the band released a cover of the iconic Brady Bunch song, "Sunshine Day" featuring Greg Brady's actor, Barry Williams. Throughout summer 2024, the band embarked on the Ride On Tour with close to 100 shows, touring everywhere from Alaska to Hawaii with major festival stops in Mexico, Chile, Peru, and Malaysia along the way.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-63)

### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
The band joined Cleopatra Records in late 2024, and released a cover of the Beatles' "Love Me Do" in November. On December 4, 2024, the band confirmed a full-length LP under the working title _Fush Yu Too_ was in the works and was to be due by the end of February.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-65) Prior to that in March, during the Ride On Tour, the band hinted going back to the studio to record an LP in the same ska style as "_Fush Yu Mang_".[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-66) On January 21, 2025, the band released a cover of "Blinding Lights" by the Weeknd, with which the band had received backlash for using AI for the cover art. It was later confirmed that the cover, as well as "Love Me Do", would be included on Cleopatra's compilation album, _Punk Rock Valentines_, which released on February 7.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-67)

### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
On March 3, 2025, the band announced the Mercury Comet Tour.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-68) A day later, on March 4, they announced their new LP was titled _Mercury Comet_ and would release in June,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-69) before being delayed indefinitely. Much like "Blinding Lights", its initial cover art received backlash for its use of AI. In March 2026, the album was finally announced to be releasing on August 12, 2026.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-70) On June 10, 2026, they released "Better Believer" as the lead single for the album.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-71)
Earlier in their career, Smash Mouth was part of the ska punk scene.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-73) After the success of their single, "Walkin' on the Sun", the band began including more elements of psychedelic pop and other retro styles of the 1960s in their compositions. They would ultimately come to be known as a pop rock,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-74)power pop[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-75) and alternative rock band,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-76) despite still retaining some elements of their ska and reggae roots.

texts.1: **Smash Mouth** is an American rock band from San Jose, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-3) The band was formed in 1994[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-4) and was originally composed of Steve Harwell (lead vocals), Kevin Coleman (drums), Greg Camp (guitar), and Paul De Lisle (bass). Harwell's departure in 2021 left De Lisle as the sole remaining original member. They are known for their songs "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" (1997), "All Star" (1999),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-5) and "Then the Morning Comes" (1999), as well as [a cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer_(Smash_Mouth_song) "I'm a Believer (Smash Mouth song)") of Neil Diamond's "[I'm a Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer "I'm a Believer")" (2001).
texts.2:
The band adopted retro styles covering several decades of popular music. They have also performed numerous covers of popular songs, including War's "[Why Can't We Be Friends?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends%3F_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends? (song)")", Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up", Simple Minds' "[Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_(Forget_About_Me) "Don't You (Forget About Me)")", ? & the Mysterians' "[Can't Get Enough of You Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Get_Enough_of_You_Baby "Can't Get Enough of You Baby")", the Beatles' "Getting Better", Queen's "Under Pressure", House of Pain's "Jump Around", and "[I Wan'na Be Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wan'na_Be_Like_You "I Wan'na Be Like You")" from _The Jungle Book_. They also composed two songs for the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_: "Beside Myself" and "Everything Just Crazy".
The group's debut album _Fush Yu Mang_ has been certified platinum twice by the RIAA and their second album _Astro Lounge_ has since been certified platinum thrice. Their song "All Star" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 2001.
Smash Mouth's roots trace back to 1990 when Steve Harwell and Kevin Coleman met. Smash Mouth was then formed in 1994 by Harwell, who had formerly played in a rap group called F.O.S. (Freedom of Speech). Coleman, who was Harwell's manager, knew guitarist Greg Camp and bassist Paul De Lisle, who had both played in a local punk band, and introduced the three musicians to each other. They began rehearsing together along with Coleman, who played drums. They soon developed into a band, and named themselves Smashmouth, an American football term. During their early years, the band played largely rock music.
texts.3: The band's first publicity came when a demo of the song "Nervous in the Alley" was played by a San Jose radio station, KOME. Soon after, Interscope Records signed the band, and the group's debut album, _Fush Yu Mang_, was released in 1997, featuring another member: the keyboardist Michael Klooster. Also, upon signing to Interscope Records, the band changed their name from Smashmouth to Smash Mouth. The album saw commercial success peaking at number 19 on the US Billboard 200 and number 23 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6) It was led by the band's first major single "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" which peaked at number 1 on the US Adult Top 40 and Alternative Songs charts and at number 3 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-7) The singles "The Fonz" and a cover of "[Why Can't We Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends (song)")" from the 1998 Kevin Bacon film _Wild Things_ were also subsequently released. The album has since gone double platinum. During this time the band officially started touring regularly even opening for U2 on their PopMart Tour and got their first television appearance as the musical guest on episode 157 of _Oddville, MTV._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-8)
texts.4:
### 1998–2004: rise to fame, _Astro Lounge_, _Smash Mouth_, and _Get the Picture?_
[edit | edit source]
The band's second album, _Astro Lounge_, was released in 1999 and marked a change in direction, as it had less of the previous ska influence and more of a pop sound. It led to more publicity for the band, and ended up being one of the most critically acclaimed albums from the group. It peaked at number 6 on the US Billboard 200, the highest the band has ever charted in the states, and reached the top 20 in both Canada and New Zealand.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-9) Supported by the hit single "All Star" (which was featured in several film soundtracks, most notably in _Shrek_ (2001), although the official music video references _Mystery Men_) the song reached number 4 on both the Billboard hot 100 and Australia it then charted even higher in Canada peaking at number 2.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-10) "Then the Morning Comes" was also a hit for the band and peaked a number 11 on the Billboard hot 100.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)_Astro Lounge_ has since been certified as triple platinum.
texts.11:
### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
In June 2011, a writer at Something Awful offered $20 if the band's lead singer, Steve Harwell, would eat 24 eggs.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Hendren_2011-27) Others on Twitter began offering additional sums, eventually targeted to various charities.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Hendren_2011-27) In July 2011, Harwell accepted the challenge if fans could gather pledges of $10,000 for [St. Jude Children's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Jude_Children's_Hospital "St. Jude Children's Hospital").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-28) The fundraising goal was reached in less than a week.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-29) A self-styled "reality TV fan", Harwell requested that his friend celebrity chef Guy Fieri prepare the eggs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-30) The event was held at Johnny Garlic's restaurant, in Dublin, California, on October 11, 2011. With about 150 people attending, Harwell was able to finish the eggs with the help of audience members as well as the San Jose Sharks mascot, Sharkie. $15,000 was raised for charity.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-31)
On July 17, 2011, Smash Mouth performed live at the Hard Rock Cafe on the Vegas Strip, airing a 60-minute concert simultaneously across the US & Canada on HDNet Television, CBS Radio, and CBS Digital.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-32)
Smash Mouth at Kinser Fest in 2013
texts.12:
### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
After parting ways with Universal Records and signing with 429 Records, Smash Mouth released their sixth studio album titled _Magic_, on September 4, 2012. The album was primarily produced by new band member Mike Krompass. The first single, also entitled "Magic", debuted on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart at No. 22.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-33) The band spent the rest of 2012 touring behind the new project as well as promoting the release of their musical book of food recipes and things of the like — _Recipes from the Road_. Cooke temporarily left again toward the end of 2012, replaced by Paxson. In 2013 the band took part in the "Under the Sun" tour with Gin Blossoms and Sugar Ray.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-34) Paxson left in July during the tour, and was initially going to be replaced by a returning Cooke; however, he was replaced by Sutter once again. Tod Burr, former drum tech of Def Leppard and drummer of Merle Jagger, came on board in 2012 as drum and keyboard tech of Smash Mouth.
On February 1, 2013, Smash Mouth headlined the AutoNation Coast to Coast rebranding event (which combined all AutoNation dealerships into a single brand) at Wayne Huizenga Park in Fort Lauderdale, Florida with Michela Paige from Season 3 of _The Voice_. The event also served as a final round in the AutoNation Culture of Caring Contest. They also took part in the first "Under the Sun" tour alongside Sugar Ray, Gin Blossoms, and Vertical Horizon.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-35)
On October 6, 2014, Smash Mouth composed two songs for the English version of the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_, including "Beside Myself", and "Everything Just Crazy" which plays at the end credits.
texts.13:
### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
In 2014, Smash Mouth was part of the second "Under the Sun" tour with Uncle Kracker, Blues Traveler, and Sugar Ray.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-36)
On June 14, 2015, Smash Mouth performed at the Taste of Fort Collins food festival in Fort Collins, Colorado. Before the encore, in an incident that lasted about three minutes, singer Steve Harwell became angry, yelled profanities at the audience, and left the stage after bread that had been distributed by the festival was thrown in the air and a few pieces were reportedly thrown onto the stage.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-37) Harwell later apologized for the incident in an interview with _The Herald-Mail_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-38) Event organizer Jason Ornstein explained that he asked Harwell if he wanted him to have the DJs make an announcement instructing the crowd not to throw bread but according to Ornstein, Harwell "stormed on [stage] and took matters into his own hands". He continued "It wasn't like anyone was going to be getting hurt by throwing bread up in the air ... We just had to laugh at it, because he just really made a fool of himself."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Sexton_2015-39) Fort Collins Police Services stated laws prohibiting disorderly conduct, harassment, and "throwing of "missiles", i.e. objects, apply to event attendees.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Sexton_2015-39)
In May 2016, Smash Mouth released their first live album titled _Playlist: The Very Best of Smash Mouth_ through Sony Music. The recordings were harvested from shows in Rapid City, South Dakota, and Manila.
texts.14:
### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
2016 saw the band gain a new member in Sam Eigen and the return of Cooke. Eigen is a long-time friend of both Steve Harwell and Paul De Lisle, and has played with Alanis Morissette, Janet Jackson, and John Fogerty. He can also be heard playing guitar on several of Harwell's solo recordings over the years.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-40)
Smash Mouth performed at the Urbana Sweetcorn Festival on August 28, 2016; Harwell passed out in the middle of the set and was taken to a nearby hospital, but the band continued their set and performed the song without him. Harwell made a full recovery and they continued touring.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-41)
Greg Camp rejoined Smash Mouth in early 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-42) An acoustic re-recording of Smash Mouth's first album, _Fush Yu Mang_, funded through PledgeMusic was released in 2018 for the album's 20th anniversary.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-43)
texts.18:
### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
On November 6, 2023, the band announced their second Christmas album, _Missile Toes_, which released on November 17. The album consists of 10 songs, six of which are covers of classic Christmas songs, and four of which are originals. Featured artists Susanna Hoffs and Sophie Grey make appearances.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-62)
Zach Goode during a show in Orlando, Florida in 2025
On April 12, 2024, Smash Mouth released the single and video "Ride On", and on July 12, the band released a cover of the iconic Brady Bunch song, "Sunshine Day" featuring Greg Brady's actor, Barry Williams. Throughout summer 2024, the band embarked on the Ride On Tour with close to 100 shows, touring everywhere from Alaska to Hawaii with major festival stops in Mexico, Chile, Peru, and Malaysia along the way.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-63)
texts.19:
### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
The band joined Cleopatra Records in late 2024, and released a cover of the Beatles' "Love Me Do" in November. On December 4, 2024, the band confirmed a full-length LP under the working title _Fush Yu Too_ was in the works and was to be due by the end of February.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-65) Prior to that in March, during the Ride On Tour, the band hinted going back to the studio to record an LP in the same ska style as "_Fush Yu Mang_".[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-66) On January 21, 2025, the band released a cover of "Blinding Lights" by the Weeknd, with which the band had received backlash for using AI for the cover art. It was later confirmed that the cover, as well as "Love Me Do", would be included on Cleopatra's compilation album, _Punk Rock Valentines_, which released on February 7.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-67)
texts.20:
### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
On March 3, 2025, the band announced the Mercury Comet Tour.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-68) A day later, on March 4, they announced their new LP was titled _Mercury Comet_ and would release in June,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-69) before being delayed indefinitely. Much like "Blinding Lights", its initial cover art received backlash for its use of AI. In March 2026, the album was finally announced to be releasing on August 12, 2026.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-70) On June 10, 2026, they released "Better Believer" as the lead single for the album.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-71)
Earlier in their career, Smash Mouth was part of the ska punk scene.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-73) After the success of their single, "Walkin' on the Sun", the band began including more elements of psychedelic pop and other retro styles of the 1960s in their compositions. They would ultimately come to be known as a pop rock,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-74)power pop[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-75) and alternative rock band,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-76) despite still retaining some elements of their ska and reggae roots.

**Smash Mouth** is an American rock band from San Jose, California.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-3) The band was formed in 1994[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-4) and was originally composed of Steve Harwell (lead vocals), Kevin Coleman (drums), Greg Camp (guitar), and Paul De Lisle (bass). Harwell's departure in 2021 left De Lisle as the sole remaining original member. They are known for their songs "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" (1997), "All Star" (1999),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-5) and "Then the Morning Comes" (1999), as well as [a cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer_(Smash_Mouth_song) "I'm a Believer (Smash Mouth song)") of Neil Diamond's "[I'm a Believer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm_a_Believer "I'm a Believer")" (2001).

The band adopted retro styles covering several decades of popular music. They have also performed numerous covers of popular songs, including War's "[Why Can't We Be Friends?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends%3F_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends? (song)")", Rick Astley's "Never Gonna Give You Up", Simple Minds' "[Don't You (Forget About Me)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_You_(Forget_About_Me) "Don't You (Forget About Me)")", ? & the Mysterians' "[Can't Get Enough of You Baby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Get_Enough_of_You_Baby "Can't Get Enough of You Baby")", the Beatles' "Getting Better", Queen's "Under Pressure", House of Pain's "Jump Around", and "[I Wan'na Be Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wan'na_Be_Like_You "I Wan'na Be Like You")" from _The Jungle Book_. They also composed two songs for the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_: "Beside Myself" and "Everything Just Crazy".
The group's debut album _Fush Yu Mang_ has been certified platinum twice by the RIAA and their second album _Astro Lounge_ has since been certified platinum thrice. Their song "All Star" was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals in 2001.
Smash Mouth's roots trace back to 1990 when Steve Harwell and Kevin Coleman met. Smash Mouth was then formed in 1994 by Harwell, who had formerly played in a rap group called F.O.S. (Freedom of Speech). Coleman, who was Harwell's manager, knew guitarist Greg Camp and bassist Paul De Lisle, who had both played in a local punk band, and introduced the three musicians to each other. They began rehearsing together along with Coleman, who played drums. They soon developed into a band, and named themselves Smashmouth, an American football term. During their early years, the band played largely rock music.

The band's first publicity came when a demo of the song "Nervous in the Alley" was played by a San Jose radio station, KOME. Soon after, Interscope Records signed the band, and the group's debut album, _Fush Yu Mang_, was released in 1997, featuring another member: the keyboardist Michael Klooster. Also, upon signing to Interscope Records, the band changed their name from Smashmouth to Smash Mouth. The album saw commercial success peaking at number 19 on the US Billboard 200 and number 23 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6) It was led by the band's first major single "[Walkin' on the Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkin'_on_the_Sun "Walkin' on the Sun")" which peaked at number 1 on the US Adult Top 40 and Alternative Songs charts and at number 3 in Canada.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-7) The singles "The Fonz" and a cover of "[Why Can't We Be Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Can't_We_Be_Friends_(song) "Why Can't We Be Friends (song)")" from the 1998 Kevin Bacon film _Wild Things_ were also subsequently released. The album has since gone double platinum. During this time the band officially started touring regularly even opening for U2 on their PopMart Tour and got their first television appearance as the musical guest on episode 157 of _Oddville, MTV._[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-8)

### 1998–2004: rise to fame, _Astro Lounge_, _Smash Mouth_, and _Get the Picture?_
[edit | edit source]
The band's second album, _Astro Lounge_, was released in 1999 and marked a change in direction, as it had less of the previous ska influence and more of a pop sound. It led to more publicity for the band, and ended up being one of the most critically acclaimed albums from the group. It peaked at number 6 on the US Billboard 200, the highest the band has ever charted in the states, and reached the top 20 in both Canada and New Zealand.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-9) Supported by the hit single "All Star" (which was featured in several film soundtracks, most notably in _Shrek_ (2001), although the official music video references _Mystery Men_) the song reached number 4 on both the Billboard hot 100 and Australia it then charted even higher in Canada peaking at number 2.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-10) "Then the Morning Comes" was also a hit for the band and peaked a number 11 on the Billboard hot 100.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-:0-6)_Astro Lounge_ has since been certified as triple platinum.

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
In June 2011, a writer at Something Awful offered $20 if the band's lead singer, Steve Harwell, would eat 24 eggs.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Hendren_2011-27) Others on Twitter began offering additional sums, eventually targeted to various charities.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Hendren_2011-27) In July 2011, Harwell accepted the challenge if fans could gather pledges of $10,000 for [St. Jude Children's Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Jude_Children's_Hospital "St. Jude Children's Hospital").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-28) The fundraising goal was reached in less than a week.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-29) A self-styled "reality TV fan", Harwell requested that his friend celebrity chef Guy Fieri prepare the eggs.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-30) The event was held at Johnny Garlic's restaurant, in Dublin, California, on October 11, 2011. With about 150 people attending, Harwell was able to finish the eggs with the help of audience members as well as the San Jose Sharks mascot, Sharkie. $15,000 was raised for charity.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-31)
On July 17, 2011, Smash Mouth performed live at the Hard Rock Cafe on the Vegas Strip, airing a 60-minute concert simultaneously across the US & Canada on HDNet Television, CBS Radio, and CBS Digital.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-32)
Smash Mouth at Kinser Fest in 2013

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
After parting ways with Universal Records and signing with 429 Records, Smash Mouth released their sixth studio album titled _Magic_, on September 4, 2012. The album was primarily produced by new band member Mike Krompass. The first single, also entitled "Magic", debuted on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart at No. 22.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-33) The band spent the rest of 2012 touring behind the new project as well as promoting the release of their musical book of food recipes and things of the like — _Recipes from the Road_. Cooke temporarily left again toward the end of 2012, replaced by Paxson. In 2013 the band took part in the "Under the Sun" tour with Gin Blossoms and Sugar Ray.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-34) Paxson left in July during the tour, and was initially going to be replaced by a returning Cooke; however, he was replaced by Sutter once again. Tod Burr, former drum tech of Def Leppard and drummer of Merle Jagger, came on board in 2012 as drum and keyboard tech of Smash Mouth.
On February 1, 2013, Smash Mouth headlined the AutoNation Coast to Coast rebranding event (which combined all AutoNation dealerships into a single brand) at Wayne Huizenga Park in Fort Lauderdale, Florida with Michela Paige from Season 3 of _The Voice_. The event also served as a final round in the AutoNation Culture of Caring Contest. They also took part in the first "Under the Sun" tour alongside Sugar Ray, Gin Blossoms, and Vertical Horizon.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-35)
On October 6, 2014, Smash Mouth composed two songs for the English version of the South Korean animated film _Pororo, The Racing Adventure_, including "Beside Myself", and "Everything Just Crazy" which plays at the end credits.

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
In 2014, Smash Mouth was part of the second "Under the Sun" tour with Uncle Kracker, Blues Traveler, and Sugar Ray.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-36)
On June 14, 2015, Smash Mouth performed at the Taste of Fort Collins food festival in Fort Collins, Colorado. Before the encore, in an incident that lasted about three minutes, singer Steve Harwell became angry, yelled profanities at the audience, and left the stage after bread that had been distributed by the festival was thrown in the air and a few pieces were reportedly thrown onto the stage.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-37) Harwell later apologized for the incident in an interview with _The Herald-Mail_.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-38) Event organizer Jason Ornstein explained that he asked Harwell if he wanted him to have the DJs make an announcement instructing the crowd not to throw bread but according to Ornstein, Harwell "stormed on [stage] and took matters into his own hands". He continued "It wasn't like anyone was going to be getting hurt by throwing bread up in the air ... We just had to laugh at it, because he just really made a fool of himself."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Sexton_2015-39) Fort Collins Police Services stated laws prohibiting disorderly conduct, harassment, and "throwing of "missiles", i.e. objects, apply to event attendees.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-Sexton_2015-39)
In May 2016, Smash Mouth released their first live album titled _Playlist: The Very Best of Smash Mouth_ through Sony Music. The recordings were harvested from shows in Rapid City, South Dakota, and Manila.

### 2005–2011: new label, fluctuating lineup and _Summer Girl_
2016 saw the band gain a new member in Sam Eigen and the return of Cooke. Eigen is a long-time friend of both Steve Harwell and Paul De Lisle, and has played with Alanis Morissette, Janet Jackson, and John Fogerty. He can also be heard playing guitar on several of Harwell's solo recordings over the years.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-40)
Smash Mouth performed at the Urbana Sweetcorn Festival on August 28, 2016; Harwell passed out in the middle of the set and was taken to a nearby hospital, but the band continued their set and performed the song without him. Harwell made a full recovery and they continued touring.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-41)
Greg Camp rejoined Smash Mouth in early 2018.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-42) An acoustic re-recording of Smash Mouth's first album, _Fush Yu Mang_, funded through PledgeMusic was released in 2018 for the album's 20th anniversary.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-43)

### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
On November 6, 2023, the band announced their second Christmas album, _Missile Toes_, which released on November 17. The album consists of 10 songs, six of which are covers of classic Christmas songs, and four of which are originals. Featured artists Susanna Hoffs and Sophie Grey make appearances.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-62)
Zach Goode during a show in Orlando, Florida in 2025

Throughout summer 2024, the band embarked on the Ride On Tour with close to 100 shows, touring everywhere from Alaska to Hawaii with major festival stops in Mexico, Chile, Peru, and Malaysia along the way.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-63)

### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
The band joined Cleopatra Records in late 2024, and released a cover of the Beatles' "Love Me Do" in November. On December 4, 2024, the band confirmed a full-length LP under the working title _Fush Yu Too_ was in the works and was to be due by the end of February.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-65) Prior to that in March, during the Ride On Tour, the band hinted going back to the studio to record an LP in the same ska style as "_Fush Yu Mang_".[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-66) On January 21, 2025, the band released a cover of "Blinding Lights" by the Weeknd, with which the band had received backlash for using AI for the cover art. It was later confirmed that the cover, as well as "Love Me Do", would be included on Cleopatra's compilation album, _Punk Rock Valentines_, which released on February 7.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-67)

### 2020–2023: Harwell's departure and death, arrival of Goode and _Missile Toes_
On March 3, 2025, the band announced the Mercury Comet Tour.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-68) A day later, on March 4, they announced their new LP was titled _Mercury Comet_ and would release in June,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-69) before being delayed indefinitely. Much like "Blinding Lights", its initial cover art received backlash for its use of AI. In March 2026, the album was finally announced to be releasing on August 12, 2026.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-70) On June 10, 2026, they released "Better Believer" as the lead single for the album.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash_Mouth#cite_note-71)
